entities.summary: Ram Sharan Sharma was a Marxist historian and Indologist who specialised in the history of Ancient and early Medieval India. He taught at Patna University and Delhi University (1973–85) and was visiting faculty at University of Toronto (1965–1966). He also was a senior fellow at the School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London. He was a University Grants Commission National Fellow (1958–81) and the president of Indian History Congress in 1975. It was during his tenure as the dean of Delhi University's History Department that major expansion of the department took place in the 1970s.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent Marxist historian and Indologist, Ram Sharan Sharma's work significantly contributed to the understanding of Ancient and early Medieval India. His research had a notable impact on the field of Indian history, shaping the academic landscape in India and beyond.
